label: Organic symmetry reflects equilibrium and is absent without it, as in amoeba
statement: Symmetry is highly characteristic of organic forms because they are figures of equilibrium governed by a principle of minimal energy, as in liquid films; symmetry is lacking only where equilibrium is lacking, as in the amoeba.
quote: Such symmetry is in a high degree characteristic of organic forms, and is rarely absent in living things,—save in such cases as amoeba, where the equilibrium on which symmetry depends is likewise lacking.

label: A cylindrical cell's end cap has twice the cylinder's radius and height about 0.27R
statement: Where a cylindrical cell of uniform wall tension is capped by part of a sphere, the sphere's radius is twice the cylinder's radius, the cap subtends a cone of 60°, and its height is about 0.27 of the cylinder radius (a little more than one-eighth of the diameter), proportions seen in the free end cells of Spirogyra.
quote: the normal height of the spherical cap over the end of the cylindrical cell is just a very little more than one-eighth of the diameter of the cylinder, or of the radius of the sphere. And these are the proportions which we recognise, under normal circumstances, in such a case as the cylindrical cell of Spirogyra where its free end is capped by a portion of a sphere.
scope: cylindrical cells with free spherical ends, e.g. Spirogyra and other filamentous algae

label: Unicellular forms and their asymmetries follow surface molecular forces
statement: In unicellular organisms not only the general configuration but also the departures from symmetry can be correlated with molecular forces, especially local variations of surface tension, acting in their fluid or semifluid surfaces.
quote: we have arrived at the conclusion, as regards unicellular organisms, that not only their general configuration but also _their departures from symmetry_ may be correlated with the molecular forces manifested in their fluid or semi-fluid surfaces.

label: A spiral needs a deflecting force carried by the growing body, not an external one
statement: A deflecting force of constant direction acting from outside, such as wind or gravity, can only bend a growing structure towards a limiting direction and never into a spiral; a spiral arises only when the deflecting force is intrinsic to the growing body and turns with the direction of growth, as the columellar muscle does in the snail-shell.
quote: the growing curve will tend to wind round and round its point of origin. In the typical case of the snail-shell, such an intrinsic force is manifestly present in the action of the columellar muscle.
scope: spirally growing shells and other growing structures subject to deflecting forces

label: Evolution varies the whole body in correlation, not character by character
statement: Because dissimilar related fishes can be referred as wholes to the same figure in different coordinate systems, variation has proceeded on definite and orderly lines under a comprehensive law of growth affecting the whole structure, rather than by independent variation of separate parts as the usual conception of natural selection assumes.
quote: But if, on the other hand, diverse and dissimilar fishes can be referred as a whole to identical functions of very different co-ordinate systems, this fact will of itself constitute a proof that variation has proceeded on definite and orderly lines, that a comprehensive “law of growth” has pervaded the whole structure in its integrity
scope: evolutionary differentiation of related animal species

label: One transformation accounts for the differences between porcupine-fish and sunfish
statement: Deforming the coordinate grid of Diodon (concentric circles and approximately hyperbolic curves) yields the outline of the sunfish Orthagoriscus, so that a single integral transformation accounts for all their apparently separate external differences while leaving the head region nearly unchanged.
quote: And as such it accounts, by one single integral transformation, for all the apparently separate and distinct external differences between the two fishes.
scope: Diodon and Orthagoriscus (Mola), and by extension related fish genera
